findings.how_to_check: In Stata, count records in tgt_flag1940.dta (it holds ~35.5M records, not 122.6M). Merge one divided file against tgt_flag1940.dta versus the full census1940_all_labeled_data.dta ID list; observe that _merge==1 against tgt_flag1940.dta includes all non-target records.
findings.suggested_fix: In tgt_fallback_diag.do, extract ids directly from histid in census1940_all_labeled_data.dta without filtering on tgt. Retain the keep if tgt optimization in 1c_tgt_divided_files.do for production matching speed, but do not use tgt_flag1940.dta as a proxy for labeled census membership.
findings.title: The diagnostic merges against target-only flags, misclassifying ~44 million labeled non-target records as absent from census1940_all_labeled_data
findings.what_the_code_does: In 1c_tgt_divided_files.do:63, `keep if tgt` filters tgt_flag1940.dta to target IDs only (~35.5M records out of 122.6M in census1940_all_labeled_data.dta). tgt_fallback_diag.do:18-21 then loads this target-only file into ids and selects records with `_merge==1` at lines 43-44, claiming at line 77: '## Divided-file records not in census1940_all_labeled_data.dta: `nn''. Because `_merge==1` captures all divided-file records not in tgt_flag1940.dta, it absorbs ~44 million labeled records with `tgt==0` in addition to the 4,819,575 genuinely absent records.
findings.why_it_matters: The diagnostic will report ~48.8 million records rather than 4.8 million records under the heading 'Divided-file records not in census1940_all_labeled_data.dta'. Its age breakdown and birthplace rankings will reflect ordinary non-target census records rather than the genuinely missing census records, completely distorting any identification assessment of selection into the target sample.

findings.how_to_check: Inspect lines 25-26 and 46-50 of MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do; notice `local ++zn' at line 47 followed by `if `zb'>1 append using `nomatch'' at line 48.
findings.title: Loop variable typo in nomatch accumulation uses zb instead of zn, causing tempfile overwrite or runtime crash
findings.what_the_code_does: At line 48 of MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do, the code executes `if `zb'>1 append using `nomatch''. Here, `zb' is the counter for files with fallback discrepancies (bad), whereas `zn' is the counter for files with unmatched records (nomatch).
findings.why_it_matters: If zb remains 0 or 1, `if `zb'>1` is never true; each file's unmatched records overwrite nomatch rather than appending, discarding all prior files and leaving nomatch with only the final file's records. Conversely, if zb > 1 before a subsequent file first encounters unmatched records (zn == 1), line 48 attempts to append to a nonexistent nomatch tempfile, crashing Stata with error 601 (file not found).

findings.how_to_check: Run tgt_fallback_diag.do on inputs where no fallback records differ; Stata aborts at line 56 with 'file __000001 not found'.
findings.suggested_fix: Guard lines 56-74 with `if `zb'>0 { ... } else { file write md \"No discrepant fallback records found.\" _n }` and lines 75-90 with `if `zn'>0 { ... } else { file write md \"No unmatched records found.\" _n }`.
findings.title: Unconditional use of bad and nomatch tempfiles crashes if zero records qualify
findings.what_the_code_does: At lines 37-41, `save `bad', replace` is executed only if `_N > 0`. If no records meet the discrepancy condition across all files, zb is 0 and bad is never created. Line 56 unconditionally executes `use `bad', clear`, which crashes Stata with error 601. Line 75 does the same for nomatch if zn is 0.
findings.why_it_matters: Once the 436 fallback discrepancies are resolved or when testing on clean datasets, the diagnostic crashes with error 601 instead of writing a clean summary, leaving the markdown file handle open.

review_limits: No paper draft was supplied; claims-vs-code review was limited to assertions and comments in the modified scripts and review brief.
External data files in $REP_F and $REP_SNU are outside the repository and gitignored; runtime execution of the Stata pipeline could not be performed.
Review was scoped to the uncommitted working tree and untracked diagnostic files as reported by git status --short, not a full-repository audit.
structured_output.summary: The target-only optimization in 1c_tgt_divided_files.do correctly preserves record-level target assignments while speeding up merges, but it directly breaks the companion diagnostic tgt_fallback_diag.do. Because tgt_flag1940.dta now contains only target IDs, the diagnostic misclassifies ~44 million labeled non-target records as absent from census1940_all_labeled_data.dta, and a loop variable typo (zb instead of zn) further corrupts tempfile accumulation. The diagnostic must be fixed to merge against the full labeled census ID universe and use the correct loop counter before running.

verified_clean.evidence: In MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:54-65, 100-103, saving only `tgt==1` in `tgt_flag1940.dta` assigns `_merge==3` (`tgt=1`) to targets and `_merge==1` to non-targets and unflagged records, which `replace tgt = 0 if _merge==1` sets to 0. Every record receives the exact same `tgt` value as before the optimization.
MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:54 defines `tgt = !(namefrst==namefrst_fs & namelast==namelast_fs)`, exactly matching the canonical definition in MATCHING/fs_avg_performance.do:80.
MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:33-42 checks `direxists` for the destination folder and `confirm file` for the flag file, halting with exit code 602 if either exists.
verified_clean.item: Pre-execution destination and flag existence guards

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/1c_tgt_divided_files.do:75-78 verifies `fT === fA`, lines 92 and 97 assert `isid id` on both sources, line 99 asserts `assert(3)` on the 1:1 merge between sources, and line 103 asserts `_N==n0` after flag merging.
verified_clean.item: Birthplace file alignment and record uniqueness assertions

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:78-83 categorizes age using `age<10`, `age>=10 & age<.`, and `age>=.`, correctly preventing missing ages from being grouped into age 10+.
verified_clean.item: Missing age handling in diagnostic age breakdown

verified_clean.evidence: MATCHING/tgt_fallback_diag.do:37-41 correctly increments `zb`, appends `bad` when `zb>1`, and replaces `bad`, correctly accumulating all discrepant records across birthplace files.
verified_clean.item: Discrepancy tempfile accumulation logic for bad records

summary.description: Two to four sentences. The overall state of the reviewed work and the single most important thing to fix. No preamble.

dimensions_reviewed.description: Which scope dimensions were actually reviewed in this run.

findings.description: Defects and concerns, ordered most severe first. Empty if none. Do not pad with stylistic observations.

severity.description: blocker: a reported result is wrong. major: a referee would demand it. minor: real but survivable. nit: cosmetic.

confidence.description: verified: traced in the source. likely: strongly implied but depends on unseen data. speculative: a question, not an established defect.

title.description: One line, stating the defect itself, not its category.

location.description: path:line, or path:line-line. Several may be comma-separated. Required: a finding without a location is not a finding.

what_the_code_does.description: Precisely what the code computes, quoting the relevant expression. Contrast with what it was evidently intended to compute.

why_it_matters.description: The consequence for a number or claim in the paper. If there is no consequence, the severity is nit.

how_to_check.description: A concrete command, tabulation, or count the author can run to confirm or refute this in minutes.

suggested_fix.description: The change, specific enough to act on. Do not apply it yourself.

verified_clean.description: Things explicitly checked that were fine. This is what makes a short findings list trustworthy rather than lazy.

evidence.description: How it was confirmed, with path:line where applicable.

review_limits.description: What this review could NOT establish: data not readable, pipeline not runnable, paper text unavailable, Stata semantics not verifiable by reading. Be explicit; silence here reads as false assurance.
